result.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
result.summary: RL post-training typically produces domain experts that must then be consolidated into one model, and as new experts keep arriving, this consolidation becomes a continual process. Weight merging and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) must re-consolidate the whole model whenever an expert is added, and can erode capabilities outside the target domains. We propose Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation (CSPD), which keeps the pre-RL model frozen, distills each RL expert independently into a soft prompt, and composes experts by concatenating their prompts without joint training. A single soft prompt suffices to distill an RL expert, recovering at least 90% of the teacher's gain in 22 of 23 math, code, and agent settings. Independently trained prompts compose well. In a multi-expert setting, the average rises with every expert added, and the full composition matches MOPD (67.83 vs. 67.79). The composition generalizes best across six held-out benchmarks. Input-space adaptation adds little serving overhead, keeping throughput within 1.5% of the unadapted backbone and reaching 2.40x that of rank-4 LoRA. These results point toward continual post-training on a fixed backbone.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CSPD：冻结 RL 后的底座模型，把每个 RL 专家单独蒸馏成一个 soft prompt，并以拼接 prompt 的方式组合多个专家而无需联合训练或整体重合并，在数学、代码与 agent 任务上验证组合效果与吞吐开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 「把一种策略压成独立可拼接的输入空间 soft prompt」这一线索，可能可供核查如何把 THINK/LOOK/STOP 等推理策略封装为可组合的轻量条件向量并避免相互侵蚀；但该工作不涉及视觉推理或推理期 latent 状态生成，迁移性需自行判断。
